card.name: Buchaechum (Fan dance)
card.tagline: Korean fan dance with peony-painted folding fans
card.profile: Buchaechum is a neoclassical Korean fan dance usually performed by groups of female dancers who manipulate large folding fans painted with pink peony blossoms to create flowing formations representing birds, flowers, butterflies, dragons and waves (Wikipedia). Dancers wear brightly coloured hanbok and perform to minyo (folk song) or sanjo (instrumental solo) accompaniment. It was created in 1954 by dancer Kim Baek-bong, who drew on Korean shamanic ritual dances and Joseon court and folk dances; it is therefore a modern, not ancient, creation.
card.insight: Buchaechum gained international prominence when a Korean folk-dance troupe performed it at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City; in 1993 the Korea Dance Association designated Buchaechum a masterpiece, and on 15 October 2014 it was registered as the third intangible cultural property of South Pyongan Province (Wikipedia; Korea.net).
